items.item: The bandwidth-delay product is bandwidth times round-trip time, the data that must be outstanding to keep a path running at full speed

at.step: The bandwidth-delay product

items.item: Throughput is capped at the receive window divided by the round-trip time once congestion control has opened up, regardless of raw link speed

items.item: A classic 16-bit window field tops out at 65,535 bytes; window scaling, negotiated once at connection setup, is what lets a single flow fill a high-BDP path

items.item: Latency and throughput are independent axes: latency is set by distance and cannot be bought down, while throughput can be increased by widening the pipe or adding concurrency
